slot.brief: Match common artificial sweeteners (e.g. aspartame, sucralose, alitame, saccharin) with their structural features or use-limits.

stem: Which artificial sweetener is a methyl ester of a dipeptide and is unsuitable for foods that are heated?

verdicts.working: Aspartame is the methyl ester of the dipeptide aspartyl-phenylalanine and breaks down when heated.

working:
Aspartame is the methyl ester of the dipeptide L-aspartyl-L-phenylalanine.
It is heat-sensitive, so it is unsuitable for foods that are heated.

Independent check: Aspartame is the methyl ester of the dipeptide aspartyl-phenylalanine and breaks down when heated.
solution:
Aspartame is the methyl ester of the dipeptide L-aspartyl-L-phenylalanine.
It is heat-sensitive and decomposes on heating, making it unsuitable for heated foods.
